Here is a comprehensive, step-by-step to-do list for passing the NCLEX, broken down from the final days of nursing school to the day of the exam. 

### Phase 1: The Paperwork (Registration & Scheduling)
- [ ] **Apply to your State Board of Nursing (NRB):** Submit your licensure application and pay the required fee to the state where you want to practice.
- [ ] **Register with Pearson VUE:** This is the company that administers the NCLEX. Pay the $200 registration fee.
- [ ] **Wait for your ATT:** Keep an eye on your email for your Authorization to Test (ATT). 
- [ ] **Schedule your exam:** As soon as you get your ATT, log into Pearson VUE and pick a date. *Tip: Schedule it for 4 to 8 weeks after graduation. Don't wait too long!*

### Phase 2: Building Your Study Plan
- [ ] **Pick your resources:** Do not use more than 2 or 3 resources to avoid overwhelming yourself. Popular combos include:
   - *Question Bank:* UWorld or Archer. 
   - *Audio/Strategy:* Mark Klimek audio lectures (especially Lecture 12 on Prioritization and Delegation).
   - *Content Review:* Saunders Comprehensive Review or Simple Nursing.
- [ ] **Take a baseline assessment:** Take a readiness test on your chosen question bank to identify your current weak areas.
- [ ] **Create a calendar:** Block out study time (usually 3–5 hours a day, 5–6 days a week). Stick to it like it’s a full-time job.

### Phase 3: Active Studying (4-8 Weeks Out)
- [ ] **Do 75–85 practice questions daily:** Mimic the testing environment. Sit at a desk, put your phone away, and no music.
- [ ] **Read EVERY rationale:** This is the most important step. Read the rationales for the questions you got *wrong* and the ones you got *right* (to ensure you guessed correctly for the right reasons).
- [ ] **Create a "Cheat Sheet" notebook:** Write down facts, lab values, or concepts you repeatedly get wrong. Review this notebook once a week.
- [ ] **Practice NGN (Next Generation NCLEX) questions:** Make sure you are comfortably practicing case studies, matrix questions, and partial-credit formatting.
- [ ] **Target weak areas:** Only do deep-dive content review on areas you are continuously scoring poorly in (e.g., if you are great at OB but bad at Pharm, stop studying OB and focus entirely on Pharm).
- [ ] **Take readiness exams:** Take a comprehensive predictor test every 1.5 to 2 weeks to track your probability of passing.

### Phase 4: The Final Week
- [ ] **Memorize the core lab values and formulas:** Potassium, Sodium, Calcium, Magnesium, BUN, Creatinine, pH levels, etc.
- [ ] **Review your "Cheat Sheet" notebook** one last time.
- [ ] **Fix your sleep schedule:** Start waking up at the exact time you will need to wake up on test day.
- [ ] **Plan your test day logistics:** Know exactly where the testing center is, where you will park, and how long the commute takes. Lay out your clothes and required ID (make sure the name on your ID exactly matches your ATT).
- [ ] **The Day Before the Exam:** **DO NOT STUDY.** Close your books at 5 PM two days before the exam. On the day before, watch a movie, exercise, eat your favorite food, and relax your brain.

### Phase 5: Test Day
- [ ] **Eat a high-protein breakfast:** Avoid heavy carbs that will make you sleepy. Limit caffeine if it makes you anxious.
- [ ] **Arrive 30 minutes early.**
- [ ] **Hide your timer and question count:** Once you sit down, consider hiding the question number on your screen. Assume you are going to take all 150 questions. If it shuts off at 85, it’s a pleasant surprise!
- [ ] **Take your breaks:** When the computer asks if you want a break, take it. Drink water, use the restroom, stretch, and reset your mind. 
- [ ] **Breathe and conquer:** Remember that safety is the core of the NCLEX. Always ask yourself: *"Which answer keeps the patient the safest?"*
